title: A Protocol for the Machine
premise: On the fringe colony of Meridian's Rest, Beatrix Montrose quietly maintains a navigation beacon that no one remembers commissioning—a beacon that actually broadcasts the loop of Earth's final transmission, keeping two hostile fleets in stalemate by convincing each side the other still holds Earth. When the colony's children begin sharing a dream of a 'singing tower,' their questions draw attention to Beatrix and the beacon, forcing her out of decades of deliberate invisibility. As investigators from both fleets converge, Beatrix must decide whether truth or peace matters more, and she finds unexpected allies in the children and their ragtag guardians, a found family she never meant to build. In the end, she rewrites the transmission itself—turning the lie into an honest warning—so the fleets stand down not through deception but through shared grief, and Beatrix finally lets herself be known.
about_author: Lior Okonkwo is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating 'impossible' losses before turning to fiction full-time. They write from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where they claim the fog does half the plotting.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Beatrix Montrose, POV. Opening on Meridian's Rest, we follow Beatrix through her meticulous routines: investigating a staged cargo accident by day, servicing the anonymous beacon by night. Flashbacks hint at why she chose invisibility after Earth went silent. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking old guilt.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Beatrix and ten-year-old Sefu Adeyemi. Children across the colony report identical dreams of a singing tower; Sefu sketches it—it's unmistakably Beatrix's beacon. Beatrix realizes the beacon's carrier wave is bleeding into young neural implants. Emotional beat: dread blooming under quiet skies.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident, Filed Under Fate
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. An insurance case turns sinister when the 'accident' damaged the beacon's relay array—the first targeted strike in years. She repairs it while dodging questions from colony administrator Vashti Okafor, who has started pulling old commissioning records. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: New POV: Fleet investigator Darius Venn of the Concordance arrives hunting saboteurs, with a rival Halcyon Pact agent, Ilsa Rehn, close behind. Both believe the other side holds Earth hostage; both sense the beacon matters. Beatrix plays the dull bureaucrat. Emotional beat: performance as survival.

chapters.title: What the Tower Sang
chapters.summary: Sefu POV. The children, led by Sefu, sneak to the beacon at night and hear the dream-song directly: fragments of Earth's last broadcast woven into the signal. They befriend the 'tower lady' instead of exposing her. Emotional beat: found family taking root in secret.

chapters.title: The Commissioning File
chapters.summary: Vashti POV. Vashti finds the file: the beacon was commissioned by Beatrix herself, forty years ago, using forged authority—and its signal is the only thing keeping the fleets from burning the colony to reach 'Earth.' Confrontation between Vashti and Beatrix ends in uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: the cost of a necessary lie named aloud.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Alternating Beatrix/Venn POV. Venn corners Beatrix; Ilsa raids the same night, and the beacon takes critical damage mid-confrontation. The children shelter Beatrix in the settlement's underlevels while the fleet agents circle. Emotional beat: trust tested under pressure; the family holds.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends at Dawn
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. With hours before the transmission loop decays and both fleets interpret silence as attack, Beatrix races to rebuild the beacon. Sefu and the children carry parts through storm drains; Vashti stalls the investigators with bureaucratic theater. Emotional beat: desperate, communal hope against a countdown.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Machine
chapters.summary: Climax, Beatrix POV. At the console, Beatrix chooses not to restore the lie but to rewrite the protocol: broadcasting Earth's true last transmission—unencrypted grief—to both fleets at once. Venn and Ilsa receive it simultaneously; weapons stand down as both sides realize they mourned the same world. Emotional beat: truth as disarmament.

chapters.title: Known
chapters.summary: Sefu POV closing into shared epilogue voice. Weeks later, the colony negotiates openly with both fleets; the beacon now sings as a memorial, and children visit it freely. Beatrix, no longer invisible, teaches Sefu the maintenance routines. Emotional beat: belonging earned, guilt released, the family made official.
